# Ariadne CF-D2 Workflow Incident Diagnosis and Fluidity Repair — Independent Verification Review

## Executive Summary

Independent verification of candidate `018099dd6c5f0502121360732feb602252eb34cc` against baseline `d1e8d31e79d8af1f5e9fa4ea6b5e68f22aaa1e3b` on branch `codex/cf-d2-workflow-fluidity-repair-gemini-review` in worktree `C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190` confirms that no P0, P1, or P2 defect exists.

The workflow repair accurately diagnoses the CF-D2 incident without overclaiming, separates hard safety controls from adaptive flow, mechanizes diagnostic hypothesis discrimination, fixes the provider tool-schema dialect (replacing tuple-only `prefixItems` with provider-admissible `items`), enforces strict local command-manifest verification, makes continuation events discoverable via CLI, and enforces machine-resolved Git commit identities.

All nine manifest commands executed in exact order with exit code 0, leaving the worktree completely clean at candidate HEAD `018099dd6c5f0502121360732feb602252eb34cc`.

---

## Detailed Evaluation against the Six Verification Criteria

### 1. Diagnosis Distinction and Scope
- [docs/ariadne-cf-d2-workflow-incident-diagnosis.md](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/docs/ariadne-cf-d2-workflow-incident-diagnosis.md#L7-L24) explicitly distinguishes genuine PostgreSQL integration complexity from workflow amplification.
- It clearly acknowledges that the underlying PostgreSQL anchor issue remains unproved and unresolved (`The unresolved PostgreSQL anchor cause remains unknown. This diagnosis is of the workflow incident, not a substitute database diagnosis.`).
- It avoids claiming an unproved exclusive cause, fulfilling criterion 1.

### 2. Hard Controls vs. Adaptive Flow
- [evidence_led_workflow.yaml](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/orchestration/harness_settings/evidence_led_workflow.yaml#L3-L28) cleanly separates `hard_controls` (rehydration, explicit authority/data/effect/stop/cleanup boundaries, protected evidence closure, immutable attempts, default denial, clean worktrees, protected ref closure) from `adaptive_flow` (single active plan/contract, single final risk-triggered veto, local repairs before dispatch, single receipt per continuation event).
- Hard safety boundaries are strictly preserved while administrative friction is reduced.

### 3. Hypothesis Discrimination and Command Enforcement in Evidence Gate
- [scripts/ariadne_evidence_gate.py](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/scripts/ariadne_evidence_gate.py#L187-L310) (`assess_diagnostic_packet`) evaluates hypothesis discrimination via `_observation_map`. If viable hypotheses do not yield distinct next observations, it returns `revision_required` with reason `correction_would_not_create_discriminating_evidence`.
- `admit_command_results` ([scripts/ariadne_evidence_gate.py](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/scripts/ariadne_evidence_gate.py#L142-L176)) enforces exact match on command length, command IDs, exact `argv` sequences, exact execution order, and requires exit code 0 for a `pass` decision. Substituted, reordered, or nonzero exit commands are rejected.

### 4. Antigravity Provider Schema & Local Egress Enforcement
- [scripts/ariadne_antigravity.py](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/scripts/ariadne_antigravity.py#L81-L96) (`structured_decision_schema`) replaces tuple-only `prefixItems` with a uniform `items` object schema admissible by the Gemini API provider dialect.
- Strict local validation (`admit_command_results` and `parse_structured_decision`) retains deterministic enforcement of command ID, exact `argv` array, ordering, and zero exit codes after structured response egress.

### 5. Event Discovery and Machine-Resolved Git Identities
- [scripts/ariadne_orchestrator_preflight.py](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/scripts/ariadne_orchestrator_preflight.py#L30-L44) provides `--list-continuation-events` to expose the exact configured continuation event vocabulary directly from `orchestrator_requirements.yaml`.
- [evidence_led_workflow.yaml](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/orchestration/harness_settings/evidence_led_workflow.yaml#L41-L44) and [verifier_execution_policy.yaml](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/orchestration/harness_settings/verifier_execution_policy.yaml) (along with AER-0286 in revision 254) require full SHA-256 commit IDs to be resolved with `git rev-parse HEAD` and reverified by worktree preflight rather than manually completed from memory.

### 6. Backward Compatibility for Manifest-Free Callers
- [scripts/ariadne_antigravity.py](file:///C:/Users/sarashera/EMR4-worktrees/r190/scripts/ariadne_antigravity.py#L62-L64) (`structured_decision_schema(command_manifest=None)`) and `parse_structured_decision` retain full compatibility for verifier calls that do not bind a command manifest.

| **C03** | `["python", "-m", "pytest", "-q", ... (flow tests)]` | 0 | 46 passed |
